steps.title: Every column with *
steps.prompt:
The star ( * ) means 'every column'.
Here we open the whole categories table and take every column it has.
steps.memory_trick: * = all the columns, in table order.

steps.title: Read the id column
steps.prompt:
SELECT chooses the COLUMNS you see.
Ask for just the id column from the categories table.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT id FROM categories;
hints: FROM names the table you read from.
steps.memory_trick: You get back only the column you name.

steps.title: Read the name column
steps.prompt:
SELECT chooses the COLUMNS you see.
Ask for just the name column from the categories table.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT name FROM categories;
hints: FROM names the table you read from.
steps.memory_trick: You get back only the column you name.

steps.title: Read the description column
steps.prompt:

steps.task: Try typing: SELECT description FROM categories;
hints: FROM names the table you read from.
steps.memory_trick: You get back only the column you name.

steps.title: Two columns at once
steps.prompt:
List columns after SELECT, separated by commas.
Here we ask for id and name together.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT id, name FROM categories;
hints: Write: SELECT id, name FROM categories;
steps.memory_trick: A comma says 'and also show me this'.

steps.title: Three columns
steps.prompt: More columns, same idea - just keep adding commas.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT id, name, description FROM categories;
hints: Write: SELECT id, name, description FROM categories;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT id, name, description FROM categories;
